title: How Light Travels
seo_title: Year 6 Science: How Light Travels Worksheets (Light Sources, Straight Lines, Opaque)
standard_text: Recognise that light appears to travel in straight lines.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on how light travels: light sources and reflectors, straight lines, transparent, translucent and opaque materials, and the speed of light. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: It comes from a source and goes straight until something reflects or blocks it.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light travels from a source in straight lines.

  • Light sources give out their own light (the Sun, a flame, a lit bulb). The Moon and mirrors only reflect light.
  • Transparent materials let light through; translucent let some through; opaque let none through.
  • Light is very fast: about 300,000 km per second. That is why we see lightning before we hear thunder (about 3 seconds per km).
Example

Is the Moon a light source?

It does not make its own light

Answer: No, it reflects sunlight.

Example

Thunder 12 seconds after lightning. Distance?

12 ÷ 3

Answer: about 4 km

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Moon or a mirror is a light source.
  • Thinking light can bend around corners on its own.
  • Mixing up translucent (some light) and transparent (clear).

faq.a: Light travels in straight lines from its source until it hits something that reflects it, lets it through or blocks it.

faq.q: Is the Moon a light source?
faq.a: No. The Moon does not make its own light. We see it because it reflects light from the Sun.

faq.q: What is the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque?
faq.a: Transparent materials let light through clearly, translucent materials let some light through but blur the view, and opaque materials let no light through.
